question: There has been a worrying rise in imports of small citrus fruits from South Africa in September and October. In September 2025, they reached 74 239 tonnes, 51% above the fiveyear average, and totalled 36 701 tonnes in October, 75% above that average. The situation remains similar in 2026, with imports of 60 864 tonnes reported in September, 24% above the five-year average.

Total imports have thus quadrupled between 2017 and 2025. The overlap with the start of the European citrus season is flooding the market and jeopardising the livelihoods of thousands of European producers. In light of the foregoing: 1.

Does the Commission intend to invoke the bilateral safeguard clause laid down in Article 34 of the EU–SADC economic partnership agreement and thus stop ruining our producers for the benefit of third countries?
What urgent changes to the import schedules will the Commission make to ensure preference for EU producers and curb this unfair competition?
